name: Zero Copy
description: Make accounts bigger than a program's memory

intro.promise: You'll grow a game's map past the memory limits a program has: 10 KB to create an account, 32 KB of heap. Then you'll grow a map past the heap without copying it.

steps.title: Create a map
steps.objective: Write a map account as big as one instruction can create
steps.learned: The 10 KB limit on creating an account

beats.text: Same opening as every Anchor program: the import and the program's id.

A program works inside fixed limits: 32 KB of heap, and a cap on how big an account can be made in one go. This lesson grows a map of a game world, one byte a tile, into both. `init` creates an account by calling the System Program, and that kind of call has a limit of its own.

beats.question: What's the biggest map `init` can create?
beats.right: Yes, 10 KB. A call from one program into another can't create more than that. I've written `InitMap` with it.
why: 40 KB is fine for an account, just not in one go: `init` goes through a call into the System Program, and those stop at 10 KB.
10 MB is the most an account can ever hold. It gets there 10 KB at a time.
beats.hint: `init` doesn't create the account itself: it asks the System Program to, from inside your program.

writes.block:
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct InitMap<'info> {
    #[account(
        init,
        payer = signer,
        space = 10 * 1024,
        seeds = [b"map", signer.key().as_ref()],
        bump,
    )]
    pub map: Account<'info, Map>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub signer: Signer<'info>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

beats.typed: That's the limit, 10 KB. I've written `InitMap` with it.

beats.text: The map keeps its tiles in a `Vec`, and Anchor reads it the way it reads every account: it copies the whole account into the heap. 10 KB is only the start, though: an account can grow after it's made, up to 10 KB more each instruction.
And `init_map`. It does nothing itself: `InitMap` creates the map.

beats.question: Who pays the rent for the map's 10 KB?
options: The program, from its own balance
Nobody: accounts on devnet are free
beats.right: Yes. `payer = signer` makes the wallet that signs the call pay the rent. For 10 KB that's about 0.053 SOL of devnet SOL.
why: A program holds no balance to spend. `payer` names an account that signs the call.
Devnet SOL is free to get, but rent is still paid in it, on every byte, as on mainnet.

steps.title: Grow past the heap
steps.objective: Grow the map until the heap can't hold a copy

beats.question: Which constraint grows `map` to `len` bytes?
beats.right: Right. `realloc` resizes an account that's already there; `realloc::payer` pays the rent for the new bytes and `realloc::zero` clears them. I've written `Grow` around it, with the map's `seeds`, so only you can grow your map.
why: `space` only counts when the account is created. The map will already exist.
That creates the account if it's missing. The map will be there; it needs more room.
beats.hint: By the time it grows, the map exists. Which constraint changes the size of one that does?

writes.block:
#[derive(Accounts)]
#[instruction(len: u32)]
pub struct Grow<'info> {
    #[account(
        mut,
        seeds = [b"map", signer.key().as_ref()],
        bump,
        realloc = len as usize,
        realloc::payer = signer,
        realloc::zero = true,
    )]
    pub map: Account<'info, Map>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub signer: Signer<'info>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

beats.typed: That's the one. I've written the rest of `Grow` around it: who pays, that new bytes start at zero, and the map's `seeds`, so only you can grow your map.

beats.text: And `grow`. It fills the `Vec` out to the new size, so the map uses every byte it has. To do that, Anchor first copies the whole map into the heap.

win.headline: Out of memory at 30 KB
win.line: The account could grow. The program couldn't: `Account` copied the 20 KB map into the heap, and `resize` needed a 30 KB buffer beside it, more than the 32 KB heap holds.
win.callPanelLine: You grew the map from the Call panel until the heap ran out.

steps.explain: This step grows the map with `realloc`, 10 KB at a time. `Account` copies the map into the 32 KB heap before `grow` runs, so at 30 KB the copy and its grown buffer no longer fit.

steps.title: Zero copy
steps.objective: Grow a map past the heap and write into it, with no copy

beats.text: Zero copy reads the account where it is: the program gets a view of its bytes, and nothing is copied into the heap. In return the struct has a fixed size and layout, so no `Vec`. That's a new kind of account, so a new map.

beats.question: Which line lets the program read `BigMap` in place?
beats.right: Yes. `zero_copy` lays the struct out as plain bytes and reads it in place; `unsafe` lets it take an array this long, and `#[repr(C)]` fixes the layout. 40,952 bytes of tiles, plus the 8 byte discriminator: 40 KB. I've written `BigMap`.
why: `Copy` makes copying cheap to write, not free: the account still comes in through Borsh, into the heap.
`Box` moves the copy to the heap, and at 40 KB the heap is too small for it.
beats.hint: You don't want a smaller copy. You want no copy.
beats.typed: That's the attribute. I've written `BigMap` under it: 40 KB with its discriminator.

beats.text: A zero copy account comes in through `AccountLoader` instead of `Account`: the map's two, to create and grow, and one to write. Each checks the big map's `seeds`, so only you can change yours.

writes.block:
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct InitBigMap<'info> {
    #[account(
        init,
        payer = signer,
        space = 10 * 1024,
        seeds = [b"big_map", signer.key().as_ref()],
        bump,
    )]
    pub big_map: AccountLoader<'info, BigMap>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub signer: Signer<'info>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
#[instruction(len: u32)]
pub struct GrowBig<'info> {
    #[account(
        mut,
        seeds = [b"big_map", signer.key().as_ref()],
        bump,
        realloc = len as usize,
        realloc::payer = signer,
        realloc::zero = true,
    )]
    pub big_map: AccountLoader<'info, BigMap>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub signer: Signer<'info>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Paint<'info> {
    #[account(
        mut,
        seeds = [b"big_map", signer.key().as_ref()],
        bump,
    )]
    pub big_map: AccountLoader<'info, BigMap>,
    pub signer: Signer<'info>,
}

beats.text: And the instructions. `paint` calls `load_mut` for a view of the bytes, and copies its text into one slice of them.

chips.label: What is devnet SOL?
chips.answer: Devnet is Solana's public test network. Its SOL is free and worth nothing, so you can deploy and call as much as you like. You get it from the devnet faucet with one button; if the faucet is busy, get some yourself at faucet.solana.com.
